newsitem.title: FRANCE: Wage accords must take account of joblessness - Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Wage accords must take account of joblessness - Kohl.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl told French television people with jobs would have to make some sacrifices in order to bring down unemployment.

"Naturally it starts with wage agreements. Those who have jobs, whether they are trade unionists or employers, must take that into account and arrange wage agreements so that our products remain competitive and we can create new jobs," he said in an interview on TF1 television.
A transcript of the interview, scheduled to be broadcast at 1800 GMT on Sunday, was sent to Reuters.

"There must be solidarity between those who have a job and those who are looking for a job. I think that is imperative, especially since the sacrifices are not so great," Kohl said. "I don't see that we have made such big sacrifices up to now."
The German jobless rolls hit a post-war record of 4.66 million in January for an unemployment rate of 12.2 percent, up from 10.8 percent in December.
Kohl said certain structural characteristics such as low birth rates and longer lifespans that pose economic challenges were evident throughout the European Union.
